ModelCharacter: Gulfstar's transition into the modern motor-yacht market: a heavy deep-keel Motor Cruiser that looks like a conventional aft-deck motor yacht but behaves like a trawler, cruising around 8½ knots on modest twin Perkins diesels.
DesignLineage: The 44 Motor Cruiser was introduced in 1978 and produced through 1980.
It marked Gulfstar's move away from the earlier trawlers that directly reused motorsailer hulls and toward purpose-developed motor-yacht products.
The deep-keel hull is displacement-oriented and the standard 130-hp Perkins twins deliver trawler-speed performance despite the motor-yacht profile.
The later Gulfstar 48/49 Motor Yacht family developed the enclosed-aft-deck motor-yacht concept further and should not be conflated with this 44.
OwnershipCharacter: A substantial two-stateroom liveaboard cruiser with excellent engine-room separation and secure side decks. Twin engines are modestly powered, but 500 gallons of fuel, two heads, generator/air-conditioning spaces and large teak surfaces make restoration and annual upkeep yacht-scale.

ModelCharacter: A Canadian twin-diesel power cat prized for Great Loop and coastal cruising: shallow draft, roughly 17-foot beam, economical 100-hp-class Yanmars and two-hull accommodations deliver excellent stability and efficiency without flybridge-yacht fuel consumption.
DesignLineage: The model was initially marketed as the PDQ 34 Passagemaker and later as the PDQ 34 PowerCat with interior updates.
The hull family remained fundamentally continuous through the naming change.

OwnershipCharacter: Excellent fuel economy and redundant twin diesels, but nearly 17 feet of beam controls slip/haul-out availability. Two hulls duplicate engines, shafts and some systems; otherwise machinery is simple and accessible.
